facts.fact_text: In the afternoon of 1 December 2002, approximately 150 people assembled in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest.
The applicants were among the approximately 150 people who assembled in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest on 1 December 2002.
The police decided to disband the assembly in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest, considering that it constituted a risk to the security of the reception.
The police forced the demonstrators back to a park next to the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest.
Section 6 of Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act) requires the police to be informed of an assembly at least three days before the date of the event.
Section 14(1) of Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act) requires the police to disband any assemblies held without prior notification.
The police decided to disband the assembly in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest, considering that it constituted a risk to the security of the reception.

The applicants pointed out that it had obviously been impossible to inform the police about the assembly three days in advance, as required by Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act), because the Hungarian Prime Minister had only announced his intention to attend the reception the day before the event.

The Pest Central District Court noted that the three-day time-limit for informing the police of a planned assembly could not possibly be observed if the demonstration had its roots in an event that had occurred less than three days beforehand.
